QF.id: XIII Introduction to Forwards and Futures_37

question.text: What is 'position limit' in futures markets and how does it differ across asset classes?

answer.text: Maximum number of contracts/exposure a participant can hold — equity uses client/TM limits and MWPL (20% of free float for individual securities); currency USDINR domestic-client limit is higher of 6% of total open interest or USD 20 million; IR futures use OI/INR thresholds with a 25% cap on outstanding underlying bond
There are no position limits in any futures market — traders can hold unlimited contracts
Position limits are identical across all asset classes at Rs 500 crore
Position limits only apply to retail traders, not institutions

explanation.text: The Logic: Each market sets its own limits per Series VIII/I/IV workbooks. Equity: client-level, trading-member level, and MWPL (20% of free float for individual securities; OI-based for index). Currency (USDINR): domestic-client limit is the higher of 6% of total open interest or USD 20 million. Interest Rate futures: limits are based on OI/INR thresholds and a 25% cap on the outstanding underlying bond. Limits prevent concentration and manipulation. The Trap: All markets have position limits — they are a fundamental risk management tool. Limits differ by participant type (client, TM, FPI, MF) and by market, and several use a "higher of" formulation rather than a single fixed cap. Note: Source-backed limits from Series VIII p.167-168, Series I p.161-165 and Series IV p.234-235.
